intervals.label: operation
intervals.locator: section '1982 – 1996 LEAR: Low Energy Antiproton Ring.'
intervals.note: 1982-1996 per the LEIR history page; the CERN Courier of 17 August 2000 says LEAR "was closed in 1996 after more than 10 years of operation".
intervals.quote: Built in 1982, The Low Energy Antiproton Ring (LEAR) decelerated and stored antiprotons for various experiments throughout its 14 year lifetime.

intervals.label: closed (later converted into LEIR)
intervals.note: LEAR was dismantled from 2003 and its four main bending magnets reused in the new LEIR ring (LEIR history page).
intervals.quote: When CERN's low-energy antiproton ring (LEAR) was closed in 1996 after more than 10 years of operation

name: Low Energy Antiproton Ring
notes: Created because experiment:ps210 (first antihydrogen atoms, 1995) ran on LEAR.

summary.plain: CERN’s first slow-antiproton ring, which ran from 1982 to 1996. It supplied the beams for the first antihydrogen atoms in 1995 and was later rebuilt as a different ring.
summary.technical: LEAR decelerated and stored antiprotons (1982-1996) for fixed-target and internal-target experiments including PS210. Its main magnets were reused for LEIR.
